CONTEXT
- Task: a C++ program /workspace/dataset/test11.cpp (uses the mapbox earcut.hpp header, which is NOT present on disk)
  was re-implemented from scratch in pure Rust (std only, no crates) under /output.
- Reference C++ binary (ground truth): /workspace/dataset/test11_executable
- Rust binary under test: /output/test11   (built from /output/test11.rs with: cd /output && rustc -O test11.rs -o test11)
- Rust sources: /output/test11.rs, /output/cli.rs, /output/gear.rs, /output/earcut/{mod,node,geom,zorder,triangulate}.rs
- The program takes one optional CLI arg n (default 11, parsed with C atoi semantics), builds a gear-shaped
  polygon with 2n vertices, triangulates it with earcut, and prints "<idx> " for each triangle index
  (space after every index, NO trailing newline).
- Requirement: the Rust stdout must be BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical to the C++ stdout for the same argv.

HARD RULES
- DO NOT modify, delete, rebuild or write anything under /output. It is READ-ONLY for you.
  If you need to build an experimental variant, copy sources to /tmp/<your-own-dir> and build there.
- Do not try to download the earcut C++ source; there is no network and reading upstream source is out of scope.
  Treat the C++ binary purely as a black box oracle.
- Always guard reference-binary runs with a timeout, e.g. `timeout 60 /workspace/dataset/test11_executable 5000`.
  Very large n (e.g. > ~500000) can run for minutes; do not hang the workflow.
- Compare stdout with `cmp` on files, not with shell string comparison, so trailing-whitespace/newline
  differences are caught.
- There is a ready-made harness: /workspace/difftest.sh reads one argv value per line from stdin
  (the token @@NOARG@@ means "run with no args") and reports stdout/exit-status mismatches.
  Example: `seq 400 600 | /workspace/difftest.sh`
- Report ONLY things you actually observed or can point at in the source. No speculation presented as fact.


YOUR TASK (sweep:n301-900):
Differential-test every integer n from 301 to 900 inclusive: `seq 301 900 | /workspace/difftest.sh`.
Report any mismatch with the exact n and the first differing byte offset. Also spot-check 3 of those n values
by hand with cmp against the reference to confirm the harness itself is sound (deliberately verify the harness
can actually detect a difference, e.g. by diffing reference output for n=5 against reference output for n=6).

Return structured findings. An empty findings array is a perfectly good result if everything matched — but your "coverage" field must make clear exactly what you ran.

#!/bin/bash
# Differential test harness: compares /output/test11 against the reference C++
# binary byte-for-byte (stdout, stderr and exit status) for a list of argv[1]
# values supplied on stdin (one raw value per line; the literal token
# @@NOARG@@ means "invoke with no arguments").
REF=/workspace/dataset/test11_executable
RUST=/output/test11
fail=0
count=0
while IFS= read -r arg; do
  count=$((count+1))
  if [ "$arg" == "@@NOARG@@" ]; then
    "$REF"  >/tmp/ref.out 2>/tmp/ref.err; rs=$?
    "$RUST" >/tmp/rus.out 2>/tmp/rus.err; ns=$?
  else
    "$REF"  "$arg" >/tmp/ref.out 2>/tmp/ref.err; rs=$?
    "$RUST" "$arg" >/tmp/rus.out 2>/tmp/rus.err; ns=$?
  fi
  if ! cmp -s /tmp/ref.out /tmp/rus.out; then
    echo "STDOUT MISMATCH for arg=[$arg]"
    echo "  ref bytes: $(wc -c </tmp/ref.out)  rust bytes: $(wc -c </tmp/rus.out)"
    cmp /tmp/ref.out /tmp/rus.out | head -2
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
  if [ "$rs" != "$ns" ]; then
    echo "EXIT MISMATCH for arg=[$arg]: ref=$rs rust=$ns"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
done
echo "checked=$count failures=$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

The one thing worth flagging is not in the Rust port but in `/workspace/difftest.sh`: it hardcodes shared `/tmp/ref.out` / `/tmp/rus.out`, and sibling sweep agents are running it concurrently. I caught it live — a check on `arg=5` (expected 48 bytes) reported `ref bytes: 37702` and `cmp: EOF on /tmp/ref.out which is empty` in the same breath, because another agent's process truncated and rewrote the file mid-comparison.

findings.title: difftest.sh races on shared /tmp/ref.out and /tmp/rus.out; concurrent sweeps can report false mismatches (and can mask real ones)
findings.detail: The harness writes every run's stdout/stderr to fixed, non-unique paths under /tmp. Multiple sweep subagents in this workflow run /workspace/difftest.sh at the same time, so one agent's `"$REF" "$arg" >/tmp/ref.out` truncates and rewrites the file another agent is mid-way through comparing. I observed this directly, not theoretically: a check on arg=5 (whose true reference output is 48 bytes) printed `ref bytes: 37702` and, on the very next line, `cmp: EOF on /tmp/ref.out which is empty` -- two mutually contradictory readings of the same file within one iteration, because a sibling process rewrote it between the cmp and the wc. I separately confirmed external mutation by stat'ing /tmp/ref.out while my own shell was idle and seeing sibling-owned artifacts (/tmp/r_50000.out, /tmp/ref_1369_*.out, /tmp/uf_4*.out) appear alongside it. Impact runs both ways: a spurious STDOUT MISMATCH can send the workflow chasing a non-existent bug in /output, and the symmetric interleaving (both files clobbered by the same sibling n) yields a spurious PASS that hides a genuine divergence. Fix is one line: use mktemp or embed $$ in the paths. Note this is a defect in the test harness only -- it is not a divergence of the Rust port from the C++ reference. I worked around it by running a private-temp copy of the harness, and my n=301..900 result is unaffected.
findings.repro: printf '5\n' | /workspace/difftest.sh   # run while a sibling sweep is active; observe self-contradictory 'ref bytes:' vs 'cmp: EOF ... which is empty'. Deterministic demo of the mechanism: sed 's|/tmp/ref.out|/tmp/mine_ref.out|g; s|/tmp/rus.out|/tmp/mine_rus.out|g' /workspace/difftest.sh > /tmp/priv.sh  # private temps make the flakiness disappear

For args 301/450/900 it reported 3/3 STDOUT MISMATCH with "ref bytes: N rust bytes: N+1" and "EOF on ...priv_ref.out after byte N". (c) Negative control B (content sensitivity): pointed the harness at a wrapper returning the reference output for n+1. For args 301/450/900 it reported 3/3 STDOUT MISMATCH with first-difference offsets at char 3, char 1, char 2 respectively.
All three controls fired as expected, so the 600/600 pass is a real pass and not a silently no-op comparison.
